title: All the more + adjective / adverb
titleEn: Using All the more with an adjective or adverb

source.file: Sentence Structure 158 -「All the more + adjective _ adverb」句.pdf
omissions: English versions of Chinese-only Important Rules are faithful editorial translations.

formula: Subject + linking verb + all the more + adjective + reason / background

formulas.formula: Subject + linking verb + all the more + adjective + reason / background
Subject + action verb + all the more + adverb + reason / background
Cause / situation + make(s) / made + object + all the more + adjective

example: The task was difficult, but that made the final success all the more meaningful.
exampleZh: 這項任務很困難，但這反而令最後的成功更有意義。

examples.en: The task was difficult, but that made the final success all the more meaningful.
examples.zh: 這項任務很困難，但這反而令最後的成功更有意義。
examples.highlight: The task was difficult, but that made the final success all the more meaningful.

rules.zh: All the more 表示「因此更加……」 它並非單純表示程度很高，而是表示某個情況令另一項特質變得更加明顯。 （這份禮物很特別。） （手寫卡令這份禮物變得更加特別。）
rules.en: All the more means “consequently even more”. It does not merely indicate a high degree; it shows that one situation makes another quality more pronounced. A handwritten card, for example, can make an already special gift all the more special.
examples: The handwritten card made the gift all the more special.

rules.zh: 不可省略 the 正確： 錯誤：
rules.en: Do not omit the. Write all the more meaningful or all the more carefully, not all more meaningful or all more carefully.

rules.zh: 形容詞和副詞的用法不同 形容詞描述人或事物： 副詞描述動作：
rules.en: Adjectives and adverbs have different uses in this pattern. An adjective describes a person or thing, as in The result was all the more surprising. An adverb describes an action, as in She listened all the more carefully.
examples: The result was all the more surprising.
She listened all the more carefully.

rules.zh: 不要加入多餘的比較形式 正確： 錯誤：
rules.en: Do not add an unnecessary comparative form. Write all the more clear, all the more difficult or all the more carefully, not all the more clearer or all the more more difficult.

rules.zh: 通常要交代令程度增加的原因 常見原因表達包括：
rules.en: Normally state the reason why the degree increases. Common ways to introduce that reason include because ..., after ..., when ..., because of ..., despite ..., and but that made ....

rules.zh: 本練習不包括以下相似句型 它們可能合乎文法，但不屬於本課指定的 all the more + adjective / adverb 結構。
rules.en: This exercise excludes similar patterns such as all the more so, all the clearer, even more + adjective and much more + adjective. They may be grammatical, but they are not the target all the more + adjective/adverb structure.

benefits.zh: 清楚說明「為甚麼更加……」 這個句型能清楚說明，某個原因如何令另一件事變得更加重要、困難、吸引或令人難忘。
benefits.en: It clearly explains why something becomes even more important, difficult, attractive or memorable by showing how one situation increases another situation's effect, value or importance.

benefits.zh: 加強語氣，但不只是使用 very Very 只表示程度高；all the more 則同時說明程度增加的原因。 （這次成功很有意義。） （這個項目幾乎失敗，因此它的成功更有意義。） 第二句不但加強語氣，還解釋了成功為甚麼特別有意義。
benefits.en: It adds emphasis without merely using very. Very only indicates a high degree, whereas all the more also explains why that degree has increased. The success was meaningful describes its degree; The project almost failed, so its success was all the more meaningful both strengthens the evaluation and explains why the success was especially meaningful.
examples: The project had nearly failed, making its success all the more meaningful.

benefits.zh: 把原因和評價連接起來 你可以把一個客觀事實和自己的評價放在同一句中，令兩個意思之間的關係更清楚。
benefits.en: You can connect a fact and your reaction to it in one organised sentence.
examples: You can connect a fact and your reaction to it in one organised sentence.

benefits.zh: 避免反覆使用 even more 你不需要反覆使用 even more... because...，可以利用這個句型增加句式變化。
benefits.en: Instead of repeatedly writing even more... because..., you can use all the more to vary your sentences.

benefits.zh: 適合表達較深入的評價 這個句型特別適合描述： 某項成就為甚麼更難得； 某個錯誤為甚麼更嚴重； 某段經歷為甚麼更有意義； 某個結果為甚麼更令人意外； 某項行動為甚麼更值得欣賞。 因此，它適合用於日常說話、故事、作文、報告、評論和簡報。
benefits.en: It supports deeper evaluation: why an achievement is more remarkable, a mistake more serious, an experience more meaningful, a result more surprising or an action more admirable. It is therefore useful in everyday speech, stories, essays, reports, reviews and presentations.

sourceOmissions: English versions of Chinese-only Important Rules are faithful editorial translations.
